name: XMonitor - Moderation Queue Drain (Staging)
description:
Staging drain for the hide-replies "Moderation Queue".

ACTIVE, and must stay active. The Telegram Router's hide path enqueues rather than calling X inline, so an inactive drain means hides are accepted from the operator and then never finish.

Woken by the Postgres pg_cron job `moderation-queue-drain`, which ticks EVERY MINUTE and calls POST /webhook/moderation-queue-drain-staging only when "Moderation Queue" actually has due rows. That heartbeat replaced a 5-minute n8n Schedule Trigger on 2026-08-27 (db/migrations/2026-08-27-moderation-drain-cron.sql), so any text still saying "runs every 5 minutes" is stale — worst-case pickup latency is 1 minute, and an idle queue costs no n8n execution.

Drains inside X's real rate limit: PUT /2/tweets/:id/hidden is capped at 50 requests per 15 minutes PER ACCESS TOKEN. Quota state is read from the x-rate-limit-* response headers into "X Rate Limits"; a token with no allowance is deferred, not dropped.

PERFORMS REAL X WRITES. Every drained row hides a real reply on X and there is no undo. Do not execute it by hand against live queue rows without explicit approval.

Docs: docs/workflows/xmonitor-moderation-queue-drain-staging.md (covers both environments).

parameters.query:
-- One row per X account that has hide work due, with the quota that account
-- may spend this pass. allowance falls back to the full 50-per-15-minute
-- window when there is no observation yet or the last window has reset --
-- that is the true X limit, not an optimistic guess.
WITH due AS (
  SELECT x_user_id, count(*) AS due_count, min(not_before) AS earliest_due
  FROM public."Moderation Queue"
  WHERE status = 'queued' AND action = 'hide' AND not_before <= now()
  GROUP BY x_user_id
)
SELECT d.x_user_id, d.due_count, d.earliest_due,
       CASE WHEN r.x_user_id IS NULL OR r.reset_at IS NULL OR r.reset_at <= now()
            THEN 50 ELSE GREATEST(COALESCE(r.remaining, 0), 0) END AS allowance,
       r.remaining AS known_remaining, r.reset_at, r.observed_at,
       a.x_username, a.telegram_chat_id AS account_chat_id, a.expires_at,
       a.access_token, a.refresh_token,
       (a.x_user_id IS NOT NULL) AS has_account
FROM due d
LEFT JOIN public."X Rate Limits" r
       ON r.x_user_id = d.x_user_id AND r.endpoint = 'PUT /2/tweets/:id/hidden'
LEFT JOIN public."X Auth Accounts" a ON a.x_user_id = d.x_user_id
ORDER BY d.earliest_due;

-- RETURNING carries the token context forward. The claim step needs
-- allowance, which does not live on "X Auth Accounts", so it is echoed
-- through as $5 -- that keeps both refresh and no-refresh branches
-- arriving at "Ready To Claim" with an identical item shape.
UPDATE public."X Auth Accounts" a
SET access_token = $2,
    refresh_token = $3,
    expires_at = $4::timestamptz,
    updated_at = now()
WHERE a.x_user_id = $1
RETURNING a.x_user_id, a.x_username, a.telegram_chat_id,
          a.access_token, $5::int AS allowance;

-- Reached when quota is spent, or when a token is stale and cannot be
-- refreshed. Rows are pushed forward, never failed: nothing here says the
-- hide itself is impossible.
UPDATE public."Moderation Queue"
SET not_before = $2::timestamptz
WHERE x_user_id = $1
  AND status = 'queued'
  AND action = 'hide'
  AND not_before < $2::timestamptz
RETURNING id, reply_id, not_before;

-- Reached only for permanent auth problems: no connected account, no refresh
-- token, or X refusing the refresh outright. Retrying cannot fix any of them,
-- so the rows fail immediately instead of consuming five attempts.
UPDATE public."Moderation Queue"
SET status = 'failed',
    last_error = $2,
    last_error_code = $3
WHERE x_user_id = $1
  AND status = 'queued'
  AND action = 'hide'
RETURNING id, reply_id;

-- Atomic claim. FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED lets a second drain pass (or a
-- future console worker) take different rows instead of blocking, and the
-- outer AND q.status = 'queued' re-check means a row another transaction
-- claimed between the SELECT and the UPDATE is dropped rather than
-- double-claimed.
--
-- LIMIT $2 is the per-token allowance computed from real x-rate-limit-*
-- headers, so a pass never dispatches more requests than X will honour.
UPDATE public."Moderation Queue" q
SET status = 'in_flight',
    attempts = q.attempts + 1
WHERE q.id IN (
  SELECT id FROM public."Moderation Queue"
  WHERE status = 'queued'
    AND action = 'hide'
    AND x_user_id = $1
    AND not_before <= now()
  ORDER BY not_before, created_at, id
  LIMIT $2
  FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED
)
AND q.status = 'queued'
RETURNING q.id, q.reply_id, q.post_id, q.x_user_id, q.batch_id::text AS batch_id,
          q.telegram_chat_id, q.telegram_message_id, q.attempts;

-- One statement for the whole pass. attempts moves by a delta rather than
-- being set, so a refunded 429 cannot race the claim step that incremented it.
WITH outcome AS (
  SELECT * FROM jsonb_to_recordset($1::jsonb)
    AS o(id uuid, status text, last_error text, last_error_code text,
         not_before timestamptz, attempts_delta int)
)
UPDATE public."Moderation Queue" q
SET status = o.status,
    last_error = o.last_error,
    last_error_code = o.last_error_code,
    not_before = COALESCE(o.not_before, q.not_before),
    attempts = GREATEST(q.attempts + COALESCE(o.attempts_delta, 0), 0)
FROM outcome o
WHERE q.id = o.id
RETURNING q.id, q.reply_id, q.status, q.attempts;

-- Keeps Replies.status as the router's candidate filter reads it: 'hidden'
-- rows are excluded from the next enqueue, 'hide_failed' rows stay eligible.
WITH updates AS (
  SELECT * FROM jsonb_to_recordset($1::jsonb) AS u(reply_id text, status text)
)
UPDATE public."Replies" r
SET status = u.status,
    moderated_at = now(),
    moderated_by = 'moderation-queue-drain'
FROM updates u
WHERE r.reply_id = u.reply_id
RETURNING r.reply_id, r.status;

-- This write is what replaces the n8n workflow static-data cache. Keyed by
-- (x_user_id, endpoint), so the state follows the token rather than the
-- workflow -- defect G.
INSERT INTO public."X Rate Limits"
  (x_user_id, endpoint, limit_ceiling, remaining, reset_at, observed_at)
SELECT s.x_user_id, s.endpoint, s.limit_ceiling, s.remaining, s.reset_at, now()
FROM jsonb_to_recordset($1::jsonb)
  AS s(x_user_id text, endpoint text, limit_ceiling int, remaining int,
       reset_at timestamptz)
ON CONFLICT (x_user_id, endpoint) DO UPDATE
SET limit_ceiling = EXCLUDED.limit_ceiling,
    remaining = EXCLUDED.remaining,
    reset_at = EXCLUDED.reset_at,
    observed_at = EXCLUDED.observed_at
RETURNING x_user_id, remaining, reset_at;

-- Section 2.2 step 3. A 429 anywhere in the pass pushes every remaining
-- queued row for that token past the reset, so the next pass claims nothing
-- for it and burns no requests.
WITH tokens AS (
  SELECT * FROM jsonb_to_recordset($1::jsonb) AS d(x_user_id text, defer_until timestamptz)
)
UPDATE public."Moderation Queue" q
SET not_before = t.defer_until
FROM tokens t
WHERE q.x_user_id = t.x_user_id
  AND q.status = 'queued'
  AND q.action = 'hide'
  AND q.not_before < t.defer_until
RETURNING q.id;

-- Progress is recomputed from the queue itself rather than accumulated in
-- the workflow, so an edit is correct even if a previous pass crashed.
-- The $1 <> '' guard keeps string_to_array from producing {''} and failing
-- the uuid cast when a pass hid nothing.
SELECT batch_id::text AS batch_id, telegram_chat_id, telegram_message_id, post_id,
       count(*) AS total,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'done') AS done,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE status IN ('failed','abandoned')) AS failed,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE status IN ('queued','in_flight')) AS pending,
       min(not_before) FILTER (WHERE status = 'queued') AS next_attempt_at
FROM public."Moderation Queue"
WHERE $1 <> ''
  AND batch_id = ANY(string_to_array($1, ',')::uuid[])
  AND telegram_message_id IS NOT NULL
  AND telegram_chat_id IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY batch_id, telegram_chat_id, telegram_message_id, post_id;

parameters.content:
## Hide Reply On X: retryOnFail must stay false

X allows **50 hides per 15 minutes per access token**. "Claim Due Hide
Rows" budgets exactly that many requests from the live
x-rate-limit-remaining header before this node runs.

An n8n-level retry spends a request the claim never budgeted, which
pushes the pass over the limit and turns clean work into 429s.

Retry belongs to the queue instead: attempts, not_before, and the
exponential backoff in "Prepare Drain Hide Result". A 429 refunds the
attempt; permanent failures are never retried at all.

Pinned by tests/n8n/moderation-queue-drain-guard.test.mjs

## X OAuth client credentials

The Telegram Router keeps the X OAuth client id and secret **inline** in
its "Prepare Refresh Request" Code node. This workflow deliberately does
not copy them: it reads X_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID and X_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET
from the n8n instance environment.

If they are unset, "Plan Drain Pass" **defers** stale-token rows and
raises a developer alert. It never fails them — a missing env var is an
operator problem, not a dead reply.

Set both, or the drain can only use tokens that are still valid.

parameters.query:
-- The comparison happens IN SQL, so the shared secret never enters n8n
-- execution data at all -- only the boolean verdict does.
--
-- This replaced a Code node reading $env.MODERATION_DRAIN_SECRET. n8n Cloud
-- blocks env access inside Code nodes ('access to env vars denied'), and
-- $vars is empty on this instance, so that gate rejected every call. Vault is
-- the one place the secret lives, and pg_cron reads the same row when it
-- signs the request.
--
-- Fails closed on every path: missing header, empty header, wrong value, or a
-- missing Vault row all yield false.
select exists (
  select 1 from vault.decrypted_secrets
  where name = 'moderation_drain_secret'
    and decrypted_secret = $1
) as authorized;
